model: EMX energy meter (BACnet MS/TP and BACnet IP)
applies_to: Senva EMX, EMX-L (BACnet MS/TP) and EMX-IP (BACnet IP) three-phase energy meters.
summary: The EMX is a Senva three-phase energy meter. Analog Inputs give voltages, currents, power factor, frequency, real/reactive/apparent power and energy per phase and total, alarm and load status, pulse counts and the clock; Large Analog Values carry net, import and export energy totals. Multi-State and Analog Values set wiring, CT type, pulse outputs, alarms, scaling, clock and the on-board logger.
notes: Points from the Setup Registers and Logging Registers tables of BACnet guide 154-0041 rev0E.
EMX and EMX-L use BACnet MS/TP; EMX-IP uses BACnet IP. Pulse output MSVs 4-9 do not apply to the EMX-IP, and AV 20-AV 28 (log reset and clock set) do not exist on the EMX-L.
The guide names AI 33-35 "Net A/B/C Apparent Energy" in Wh, the same names as AI 39-41 in VAh; kept as printed.
Logging registers (AV 29-45, AI 49-78) read back entries from the on-board log.
Multistate objects are MSV in the guide; listed here as MV. All MSVs and AVs are read/write; AIs and LAVs are read-only.

integration.summary: Set wiring (MV 1), current element type (MV 2) and scaling (AV 1, AV 2) to match the installation, then read total power, energy, voltage, current and the alarm status. The meter is monitoring-only apart from resets and setup.
setup: EMX/EMX-L: BACnet MS/TP; EMX-IP: BACnet IP. Device instance defaults to 1 and is writable.
Wiring (MV 1), CT or Rogowski coil (MV 2), CT orientation (MV 3) and current/voltage scale (AV 1, AV 2) must match the install.
The EMX-L has no display; it is set up with the SenvaSync phone app.
gotchas: AV 17 resets the energy totals; AV 20 clears the log.
Clock changes (AV 21-27) take effect only after writing 1 to AV 28.
Setup values are stored in non-volatile memory; do not write them cyclically.
